data.question: Should block_k be tightened a second time, from 2 to 1, even though the gain is small and uncertain and the cost falls mainly on company C, or should the rules stay at v2?
data.background: The measured gain is uncertain: on-time deliveries rise by +1.2 on average, but only 2 of 5 seeds improve. Every company is already at an on-time rate of 0.97 or higher, so there are only about 4 on-time orders left to gain. This would be the second consecutive tightening of block_k after you adopted v2 against B's and C's votes and asked for C's utility to be re-measured, so whether shifting more cost onto C is acceptable is a fairness judgment for you, not for me or the vote alone.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 2 → 1. Measured averages: on-time 225.0 (vs 223.8, change +1.2, 2/5 seeds improved), late 3.0 (vs 4.2), blocked s 130 (vs 936), road violations 29.8 (vs 28.0), lowest on-time rate 0.98 (vs 0.97), unfinished 0.0. KPI conditions hold. Utility A / B / C becomes 73.4 / 74.2 / 40.1 (from 73.4 / 65.5 / 56.3). Votes: A ○, B ○, C ×.
options.stakeholders: B gains clearly (utility 65.5 → 74.2) and A is unchanged (73.4). C loses heavily (56.3 → 40.1), a second cost to C after v2. Customers gain slightly on average (about 1 fewer late delivery), but the gain appears in only 2 of 5 seeds, and C's customers may be affected if C's operations are squeezed. Road violations rise slightly, which affects everyone sharing the road.

options.summary: Stay at v2 (block_k 2). Measured averages: on-time 223.8, late 4.2, blocked s 936, road violations 28.0, lowest on-time rate 0.97, unfinished 0.0. KPI conditions hold. Utility A / B / C stays 73.4 / 65.5 / 56.3.
options.stakeholders: C keeps its re-measured utility (56.3) and avoids a second consecutive loss. B forgoes its gain (stays at 65.5). A is unaffected. Customers keep the current service level, with all companies already at an on-time rate of 0.97 or higher, at a cost of about 1.2 more late deliveries on average than option 2.

recommendation.reason: The gain is small (+1.2 on-time, about 1 late delivery fewer) and not reliable (only 2/5 seeds improve), while C's utility falls by about 16 points (56.3 → 40.1) and road violations rise (28.0 → 29.8). Every company already meets the fairness condition with margin (0.97 or higher), so the main KPI does not clearly justify a second tightening against C's vote. I suggest re-measuring with more seeds before reconsidering it.

unknowns: Whether the A and B yes votes alone meet the quorum, i.e. whether option 2 passes the vote without an override.
Why C's utility under v2 now measures 56.3, compared with the 19.0 reported last period (a change in measurement, demand, or C's behavior), and whether the drop to 40.1 is stable.
How results vary per seed: whether the 3 non-improving seeds got worse or stayed flat, and whether more seeds would confirm the +1.2.
Why road violations rise under block_k 1 and whether they would cause safety or rule problems.
How C will change its routing or behavior in response to a second tightening, and how A and B will act.
How C's customers and customers in general perceive the change, including any effect on C's service that the averages do not show.
Demand in the next period, and whether the small remaining margin changes under heavier load.
